blockingFindings: UNDEFINED F1 PASS PREDICATE. The pre-MC03 gate is stated as 'reviewed F0 plus successful F1', but F1 simultaneously says 'Missing suitable inputs keep the affected probe incomplete' and 'generating a missing fixture needs its own admitted bounded stage'. Nothing defines whether F1 is 'passed' when one or more of its three probe families (native transcript agreement, canonical export/import, constrained final-pairing rejection) is incomplete for want of a fixture. As written the gate is either a silent waiver (dispatch F2 on a vacuous F1) or an indefinite stall. FIX: enumerate the required F1 probes as an explicit ID list in backend-decision.json, give each a per-probe disposition (passed / failed / incomplete-with-named-missing-input), and define F1-passed as: every probe passed, OR each incomplete probe is explicitly waived with a recorded justification that names the exact F2/F3 control which absorbs the deferred obligation and the reviewer who accepted the deferral. A failed probe is never waivable.

F2 PREREQUISITES ARE OVER-BROAD AND AMBIGUOUS, GATING THE CRITICAL UNKNOWN BEHIND UNRELATED DESIGN WORK. F2 (the narrow, fixed-instance native IVC proof over an unchanged two-transition relation with frozen constants) lists as inputs 'MC01 acceptance, reviewed RP01, completed F1 discriminating controls'. RP01's own completion predicate spans the eight intent cases, eight DeFi regression classes, five composition operators and the full theorem ledger, owned by MC05/MC06/MC07 - none of which is load-bearing on the fixed native relation. 'Reviewed RP01' is also undefined as between 'gate status complete' and 'the RP01 rows relevant to MC03 reviewed'. Similarly MC01 (a TypeScript language package) acceptance is not obviously load-bearing on the Rust native harness. This risks either stalling the highest-uncertainty item (the native-to-Preview boundary, which both the PCD review and MC04 record place on the critical path) or being resolved by ad-hoc relaxation at dispatch time. FIX: state F2's prerequisite as a named minimal RP01 subset (the rows that bind the MC03 statement: relation constants, terminal row/effect semantics, predecessor identity, work-budget conservation) plus F1; record the subset IDs in backend-decision.json; and state explicitly which prerequisites are deferred to F3/F4 rather than F2. If MC01 acceptance is genuinely required for F2, state the exact dependency; otherwise replace it with the specific MC01 artifacts the native statement binds.

NO OWNER, AUDIT STEP OR RESOURCE LINE FOR AUTHORING THE F1 COMPONENT CANDIDATE. F1's inputs include 'exact implemented component candidate', but F0 forbids compilation/synthesis/proving and no stage assigns who writes, reviews and audits the new wrapper components that F1 must probe - above all the constrained final fixed-G2 pairing finalizer, the native-0.8 verifier/transcript port and the checked VK/instance/accumulator export interface, all of which the MC04 record lists as absent at the inspected pins (CLM-MC04-0203, 0204, 0205). The register's MC03/MC04 reservations (85 and 50 minutes, 3 dispatches each) are visibly inconsistent with authoring and probing a cross-version in-circuit pairing/verifier port, so F1 can only be entered on an unrecorded allocation. FIX: insert an explicit authoring stage between F0 and F1 (owner MC04, with MC03 for native-side export) whose exit criteria are: component source frozen at a hash, independent Opus and GPT-6 source review of the component (not just the design), and an RP03-recorded conservative resource estimate and stop predicate for the component build. Amend the register's MC03/MC04 reservations through the existing delegated resource decision before F1 admission rather than after.

ACCEPTANCE STEPS OMIT THE REVOCATION/ACTIVATION/MIGRATION CASES THAT RP01 MANDATES. RP01 requires specifying that 'cryptographically valid evidence under a revoked key must reject' and that 'migration cannot revive consumed history or reset work' - the disposition the PCD review derives from report lines 705/731/982-986 and 1117, and which it notes is absent from the inspected MC01-MC08 change specs. But the Execution sequence and acceptance steps 4 and 7 never carry these into MC05/MC08 completion predicates: step 7 lists stale observations, restart and conflict recovery only. A design-gate requirement with no acceptance-side obligation is not preserved scope. FIX: add to step 4 (MC05) an explicit acceptance case for an old key/spec that still verifies cryptographically but is no longer permitted, and for a scheduled activation window; add to step 5/7 a migration case that cannot resurrect a consumed predecessor or reset lifecycle/work budgets; and record these as required entries in the RP01 theorem/challenge ledger with named owners so RP01 cannot reach 'complete' without them.
nonblockingFindings: CITATION IMPRECISION IN THE DECISION TABLE. 'Intents lines 2012-2016 ... recommend optional or deferred proof integration' is loose: per the supplied excerpt, 2012 is the reserve-attestation caveat (which the plan agrees with); the deferral recommendation is 2014-2016. Likewise PCD 1113-1117 is characterized as recommending 'optional or deferred proof integration', but 1115 excludes mandatory recursion while 1117 forbids prover-selected verifiers - a position the plan adopts, not supersedes. Fix: cite 2014-2016 and 1115 for the superseded recommendations, and cite 1117 separately in the adopted column alongside 'A host verification boolean is forbidden'. DeFi 664 and 1140 and PCD 679-683 are quoted accurately against the excerpts.

THE '32 DISPOSITIONS' DENOMINATOR IS INCONSISTENTLY NAMED AND UNPINNED. The decision table says '32 taxonomy dispositions'; RP01's first bullet says '32 ACTUS dispositions'. Nothing in the supplied packet establishes what the 32 are or where they live (the 277 fixtures, 72 rows and 349 cap are corroborated by defi.review). Since this is part of a no-substitution corpus commitment, fix by naming one term, pinning an exact source path plus SHA-256 in semantic-challenges.json, and stating whether the 32 are a subset, an index over, or disjoint from the 277.

RP01 DOES NOT CARRY FORWARD TWO SPECIFIC CORRECTIONS ITS OWN SOURCE REVIEW RAISED. intents.review flags that the report's 'exact-output exchange' actually uses a minimum-output inequality, and that authority attenuation does not preserve every economic risk metric. RP01 names 'exact-output swap' without requiring the equality-vs-minimum predicate to be disambiguated, and the theorem ledger does not require the attenuation claim to be stated as the precise subset property. Fix: add both as required disposition fields on the relevant challenge and theorem rows.

MC02 IS OUTSIDE THE F0-F4 STAGE TABLE THOUGH IT CONSUMES PREVIEW SUBMISSIONS. The register reserves six Preview submissions for MC02, and the staged section says public submission requires 'the stage's explicit execution admission', but MC02 has no stage. It is honestly labelled an uncertified integration probe, yet a reader could treat its receipts as partial terminal evidence. Fix: place MC02 in the table as a parallel non-PCD track with its own RP03 admission and an explicit prohibition on citing its receipts toward the terminal acceptance predicate.

GATE-RECORD FILE IDENTITY AND PER-STAGE SCHEMA GAPS. 'All three planned gate JSONs' is ambiguous for RP01, which lists four planned files (semantic-challenges.json, semantic-decisions.md, signing-display-schema.json, theorem-ledger.json); name the single canonical gate-record file per gate and make the others referenced inputs/outputs with hashes. Separately, the staged section requires a delegated resource receipt and stop predicate per stage, but the RP02 record schema lists only per-stage status, artifacts, secret ownership, provenance and control results - add resourceReceipt and stopPredicate fields.

REGISTER DOES NOT MIRROR THE DESIGN-WORK PERMISSION. The plan states these checks add no package and that 'package dependencies still govern final acceptance', which authorizes RP01 design authorship by MC05/MC06/MC07 while their MC03/MC04 dependencies are unmet. The program register carries only planningPrerequisiteScope wording scoped to MC01 corrections. Fix: add an explicit design-work-permitted scope note to MC05/MC06/MC07 so a dispatcher implementing the RP predicates does not block RP01 authorship, and state that such authorship confers no package progress or acceptance.

PREPARATION EDITS COULD ERODE THE PINNED CANDIDATE. Editing source is permitted before proof admission, while the same section pins moriarty_loan_r3.rs and its runner by SHA-256 as starting inputs. Fix: require preparation edits on a separate branch/worktree, keep the pinned candidate immutable until RP03 records the successor hashes, and require re-review when a hash changes.

POSITIVE OBSERVATIONS (recorded, not approvals). The amendment does de-circularize the two gates most at risk: RP03 is explicitly campaign-specific and does not require a full MC07 episode manifest before an MC02/MC03 probe, and F1 explicitly does not take a complete MC03 proof as a prerequisite while assigning terminal-proof-dependent controls to F2/F3. The F1/F3 control freeze list is a faithful reproduction of the MC04 record's mutation list, including the requirement for a meaningful-state-change fixture rather than an empty call. The eight DeFi regression classes, the eight intents worked cases and the eight theorem families match the supplied excerpts. Scope non-reduction is explicit: mandatory history with no accelerator or deterministic-only fallback, total/decidable evaluation with no unrestricted recursion or unbounded callback, all 277 fixtures and 72 rows retained with 349 rejected as a coverage argument, non-mock Preview financial state change for both loan and swap, and MC06 isolated split/branch/join retained at F4.
acceptedScope: Plan-review only, on the supplied text alone. I accept, at the level of stated intent, that the amendment (a) preserves the six mandatory scope elements - Midnight-centric target with other chains as comparative research only, mandatory proof-carrying history with no optional/deferred/accelerator fallback, finite bounded totally-evaluable semantics with no unrestricted recursion or unbounded callbacks, the full ACTUS 277 / DeFi 72 corpus with the 349 cap rejected as a coverage argument, a non-mock Preview transaction producing a meaningful financial state change for both loan and swap, and MC06 real private split/branch/join; (b) directionally corrects the four report disagreements (DeFi 664 unbounded domains rejected, DeFi 1140 and intents 2014-2016 deferred/optional PCD superseded, PCD 1115 no-mandatory-recursion superseded while PCD 1117 and 679-683 are adopted, intents 2192-2194/2498-2509 NEAR/EVM/ERC-7540 adapters excluded as deliverables); and (c) uses the MC04 source record accurately, including the ledger-8 V2 versus ledger-9 V3 distinction, the absence of a constrained final pairing and checked accumulator export, and the correct framing of all of this as source inspection rather than an impossibility proof or a deployment fact. I accept the stage graph as broadly non-circular in its two most-at-risk places. I do NOT accept, and this review does not establish: any implementation, feasibility, performance or acceptance result; the truth of any external or deployment claim; the existence, contents or hashes of any referenced file; MC01 acceptance; MC03 native runnability; or that any RP gate is enforced at runtime. Nothing here authorizes native compilation, synthesis, proving or public submission.
